topic.title: An Olympic blog
topic.description: Read a blog post written during the Olympic Games to learn about sports, venues, and spectator experiences.

readingPassage.title: My Olympic Games Experience
readingPassage.text:
Day 4 of the Games has been incredible! I woke up early to catch the train to the Olympic Park. The atmosphere here is electric, with fans from all over the world wearing their national team colors.

First, we watched the gymnastics finals. The athletic ability of the athletes was mind-blowing, especially on the high bar. In the afternoon, we headed to the aquatics center for the 100m freestyle swimming. The crowd went wild when the home athlete won silver by just 0.05 seconds!

Tonight, we're taking the tube to the main stadium to watch the athletics track events. It’s been a dream come true to experience the Games live.

vocabulary.definition: The mood or feeling in a place or situation.
A facility specifically designed for water sports like swimming and diving.
The medal awarded for finishing in second place in a competition.

tips: Pay attention to chronological order markers ('First', 'In the afternoon', 'Tonight').
Look for emotional and descriptive adjectives ('electric', 'mind-blowing', 'wild') to understand spectator tone.

topic.title: Adventure travel

readingPassage.title: Extreme Outdoor Expeditions
readingPassage.text:
Trip A: White-Water Rafting in Patagonia
Navigate thrilling rapids through stunning glacier valleys. Suitable for brave beginners with strong swimming skills. All safety gear provided. (Duration: 5 days)

Trip B: Trekking the Inca Trail
Hike through high-altitude cloud forests to reach ancient ruins. Requires high physical fitness and endurance. Tents and guides included. (Duration: 7 days)

Trip C: Desert Safari & Sandboarding
Drive 4x4 vehicles across giant sand dunes and experience sandboarding under the stars. Includes camping in traditional Bedouin tents. (Duration: 3 days)

topic.title: Food and restaurants review
topic.description: Read reviews of four popular city restaurants specializing in different international cuisines.

readingPassage.title: City Dining Guide
readingPassage.text:
1. Spice Garden (Indian): Authentic street food and rich curries. Great vegan options and affordable prices, but booking is essential as tables fill quickly.
2. La Trattoria (Italian): Cozy family restaurant serving wood-fired pizzas and homemade pasta. Excellent house wine and warm service.
3. Sakura Sushi (Japanese): Sleek, modern dining with fresh sashimi and bento boxes. Slightly expensive, but perfect for a special celebration.
4. El Tapeo (Spanish): Vibrant tapas bar with live flamenco guitar. Great for sharing small plates with large groups of friends.

vocabulary.definition: Made or done in a traditional, genuine way.
Smooth, elegant, and modern in appearance.
Small savory Spanish dishes served with drinks.

tips: Scan for price indicators ('affordable', 'expensive') and dietary notes ('vegan options').
Match group sizes and dining occasions to restaurant atmospheres.

readingPassage.title: Exchange Visit Preparation
readingPassage.text:
Dear Anna,

We are so excited to welcome you to London next month for your exchange stay! My name is Mrs. Davies, and I live with my husband and our 15-year-old daughter, Sophie.

Your room is upstairs and has a desk where you can study. Sophie loves playing volleyball and baking, and she can't wait to show you around her school. Please let us know if you have any dietary allergies or preferences so we can prepare meals accordingly.

Safe travels!
Best regards,

topic.title: A friendship quiz
topic.description: Read a magazine-style personality quiz to evaluate friendship traits and loyalty.

readingPassage.title: What Kind of Friend Are You?
readingPassage.text:
Question 1: Your best friend is upset about a bad exam result. What do you do?
A) Listen patiently and help them study for the retake.
B) Tell them not to worry and distract them with a fun activity.
C) Give them space until they feel better.

Question 2: Your friend invites you out, but you are very tired. What do you do?
A) Go anyway because you don't want to let them down.
B) Explain honestly that you are tired and suggest meeting tomorrow instead.
C) Make up an excuse and stay home.

vocabulary.definition: To divert someone's attention away from something troubling.
To fail to support or satisfy someone who relies on you.

tips: Analyze scenario options for emotional and practical responses.
Understand idiomatic expressions related to personal relationships.

topic.title: How to be a safe and smart searcher
topic.description: Read an instructional guide on evaluating search engine results, online sources, and digital credibility.

readingPassage.title: Smart Online Research Guide
readingPassage.text:
1. Use precise keywords: Instead of searching 'history of cars', try 'electric car technological history 21st century'.
2. Check the domain extension: Educational (.edu) and government (.gov) websites are generally more reliable than commercial (.com) blogs.
3. Cross-check facts: Always verify news or facts across at least two independent reliable sources.
4. Look for the author and publication date to ensure information is current.

vocabulary.definition: The ending of a web address (e.g., .edu, .org, .com) indicating the site type.
To verify information by comparing different sources.

tips: Pay attention to research terminology like 'keywords', 'domain extensions', and 'cross-checking'.
Identify criteria used to determine web credibility.

topic.title: Skills for the 21st-century workplace
topic.description: Read an educational article discussing adaptability, collaboration, critical thinking, and digital intelligence in modern careers.

readingPassage.title: Essential Workplace Skills
readingPassage.text:
In today's rapidly changing economy, hard technical skills alone are not enough. Employers increasingly seek soft skills:
- Adaptability: The ability to learn new tools and adjust to changing environments.
- Critical Thinking: Analyzing information objectively rather than accepting it without evidence.
- Collaboration: Working productively across diverse remote and international teams.
- Emotional Intelligence: Understanding and managing your emotions and communicating empathetically.

vocabulary.definition: The capacity to adjust easily to new conditions or changes.
Working jointly with others toward a shared goal.

tips: Understand the difference between 'hard skills' (technical knowledge) and 'soft skills' (interpersonal abilities).
Learn key abstract nouns used in career articles.

topic.title: Tips for being a super-organised student
topic.description: Read advice on time blocking, workspace management, digital archiving, and study-life balance.

readingPassage.title: Master Your Study Schedule
readingPassage.text:
Becoming an organized student isn't about studying 10 hours a day—it's about smart planning.
1. Time Blocking: Divide your afternoon into fixed blocks for study, exercise, and hobbies.
2. Digital Backups: Save all assignment drafts to a cloud storage folder to avoid losing work.
3. The 2-Minute Rule: If a small task takes less than two minutes (like replying to an email or filing a sheet), do it immediately instead of putting it off.

vocabulary.definition: A scheduling method where time is divided into specific blocks for different tasks.

topic.title: A travel guide to Costa Rica
topic.description: Read a travel guide highlighting rainforest wildlife, volcano tours, and eco-tourism activities in Costa Rica.

readingPassage.title: Discover Costa Rica
readingPassage.text:
Costa Rica is a tropical paradise in Central America known for its incredible biodiversity and eco-friendly tourism. 

Top Highlights:
- Monteverde Cloud Forest: Walk across hanging bridges surrounded by misty trees, sloths, and exotic birds.
- Arenal Volcano: Hike near an active volcano and relax in natural geothermal hot springs afterwards.
- Pacific Coast Beaches: Perfect for surfing, turtle watching, and enjoying gorgeous sunsets.

vocabulary.definition: The variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat.

tips: Identify tourist regions and their specific nature highlights.
